name: C. Wang, 'von Laue's theorem and its applications', arXiv:1206.5618v12 = Can. J. Phys. 93, 1470-1476 (2015), eq. (20): the Gauss-law identity oint_S dS_l (Omega^{l mu} X^i) = int_V (d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i d^3x + int_V Omega^{i mu} d^3x, used by tolman.py in its divergence-free form and traced on a sphere

source.located: arXiv:1206.5618v12 (the version alphaXiv serves; its text layer carries the journal pagination Can. J. Phys. 93: 1470-1476 (2015), doi 10.1139/cjp-2015-0198, received 26 March 2015, accepted 15 June 2015). Eq. (20) is on journal p. 1474, Sect. 6. First arXiv submission 2012 (id 1206); the tree cites both the arXiv id and the CJP reference.
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true) returned the whole paper including the author's appended 'Materials to help reading'; answer_pdf_queries re-read pp. 1-7. Both are text layers of the same PDF: Greek letters and the operators in the displayed equations are lost. The operators in eq. (20) were recovered from the paper's own consistent glyph use: in footnotes 8 and 9 (p. 1472) the same two glyphs must mean '=' and '+' (Jammer's condition int Omega^11 = int Omega^22 = int Omega^33 = 0; Bialynicki-Birula's int Omega^ii = int(Omega^11 + Omega^22 + Omega^33) = 0), and the product rule printed directly above (20), d_k(Omega^{k mu} X^nu) = (d_k Omega^{k mu}) X^nu + Omega^{nu mu}, fixes the result. That recovery is an inference from the text layer rather than a glyph read directly, and it is the only form consistent with Wang's own later sentence 'from (20), with d/dt = 0 and d_nu Omega^{mu nu} = 0 => d_l Omega^{l mu} = 0 taken into account we have int_V Omega^{i mu} d^3x = 0' when the boundary term vanishes. Re-derivation C1/C2 confirms that form exactly.

published_statement: Sect. 6, p. 1474: 'From differential rules, we have d_k(Omega^{k mu} X^nu) = (d_k Omega^{k mu}) X^nu + Omega^{nu mu} and d_k(Omega^{mu k} X^nu) = (d_k Omega^{mu k}) X^nu + Omega^{mu nu}, where k, mu, nu = 1, 2, 3, and 4. With dOmega/dt = 0 => dOmega/dX^4 = 0 taken into account, from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law we have  oint_S dS_l (Omega^{l mu} X^i) = int_V [(d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i] d^3x + int_V Omega^{i mu} d^3x   (20)  (i, l = 1, 2, 3 for left-divergence and row-four-vector)', with the transposed form (21) for right-divergence, and 'If Omega^{mu nu}(x) is symmetric, (20) and (21) are the same.' Then: 'Suppose that the boundary condition oint_S dS_l Omega^{l mu} X^i = 0 holds ... Thus from (20), with dOmega/dt = 0 and d_nu Omega^{mu nu} = 0 => d_l Omega^{l mu} = 0 taken into account we have int_V Omega^{i mu} d^3x = 0.' Sect. 2, p. 1471: 'The integral domain V can be multiply connected.' Metric: g = diag(-1,-1,-1,+1), index 4 = time (Sect. 3, p. 1472). Ref. [1]: 'M. von Laue. Ann. Phys. 35, 524 (1911).'
published_hypotheses: Omega^{mu nu}(x) a (not necessarily symmetric) four-tensor in the laboratory frame, index 4 = time, metric diag(-1,-1,-1,+1)
time-independent: dOmega^{mu nu}/dt = 0 (so the 3-divergence d_l Omega^{l mu} equals the 4-divergence d_nu Omega^{nu mu})
V any spatial domain with closed boundary S (Wang: 'can be multiply connected'); X^i the position coordinates; NO ball, NO shape, NO symmetry of the source required

eq. (20) itself does NOT assume divergence-free: the term int_V (d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i d^3x is kept; divergence-free (left-divergence, first index contracted) is the specialization Wang applies afterwards

implicit, stated only as 'from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law': Omega^{l mu} X^i regular enough on the closure of V for the divergence theorem (C^1, or distributionally differentiable with integrable divergence and no interior singular sources)
Omega^{i4} = 0 is a hypothesis of Wang's von Laue theorem (Sects. 2, 6), NOT of eq. (20)
hypothesis_drift: STATEMENT FORM, not a content drift -- tolman.py:131-133 quotes 'Wang eq. (20), for a divergence-free time-independent tensor, oint_S dS_l (Theta^{l mu} X^i) = int_V Theta^{i mu} d^3x'. The published (20) is the general identity with the divergence term int_V (d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i d^3x kept. The tree's line is the divergence-free specialization, which is exactly the step Wang himself takes in Sect. 6. The tree names 'divergence-free' as a hypothesis, so nothing is dropped; it is a specialization quoted under the equation number. Re-derivation C1b shows the short form fails without that hypothesis (residual 28 pi R^5/15 for the fixture), so the hypothesis carries weight and the tree states it.

ADDED (stronger than source, in the conservative direction) -- tolman.py:566-567 'Wang's eq. (20) needs the REGION to be a ball'. The source needs no ball: V is arbitrary and 'can be multiply connected' (p. 1471). The ball, a sphere centred on the origin of X^i so that X^i = R n^i on S, is needed only by the tree's own step that evaluates the traced surface term as 4 pi R^3 <T^r_r>(R). This is a discrepancy about what the cited equation needs. It does not narrow the tree's result, because the tree only ever uses balls. C2 verifies (20) exactly on a cube.

WEAKENED AT THIS SITE, CARRIED ELSEWHERE -- tolman.py:567 'THE SOURCE MAY BE ANYTHING'. The Gauss-theorem regularity that Wang's derivation rests on ('from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law') is not named at this site: Theta must be regular and integrable throughout V, with no interior point or line singularity and no wall carrying a surface force. Read classically, 'divergence-free on V' already requires differentiability at every point of V, so the hypothesis is implicit in the tree's own 'divergence-free'. The tree also names it elsewhere: HYPOTHESES tuple tolman.py:1198 ('regular_centre', 'ball_excludes_walls') and the refusals at tolman.py:547-549 (Coulomb field: 'divergent enclosed integral -> REFUSE'; any ball enclosing a mirror). But 'regular_centre' as defined at tolman.py:931-936 (r^3 p_r absolutely continuous with a limit at 0) is a CENTRE condition. For the NON-spherical sources the Laue route admits (F5, F6), regularity has to hold THROUGHOUT V, for example at an off-centre point singularity. Re-derivation C5 shows the failure mode: for Coulomb stress the identity holds exactly on a shell a<r<R, but on the ball the LHS is -q^2/(8 pi R) and the RHS diverges. Proposed name for the hypothesis: SOURCE-REGULAR-THROUGHOUT-V. The tree's actual non-spherical witnesses are constant-stress and so regular, and no use in the tree violates the hypothesis.

UNSTATED, HARMLESS FOR THE TREE'S USES -- (20) is the LEFT-divergence form, contracting the first index. For a non-symmetric tensor, (21) (the second index) differs, and left-divergence-free does not give the second-index identity (C7). The tree's Theta is a stress-energy tensor, symmetric, so (20) = (21) as Wang notes. tolman.py:131-138 does not state symmetry, but no site uses a non-symmetric tensor.

CONVENTION, NOT DRIFT -- Wang uses g = diag(-1,-1,-1,+1), where the mixed component T^r_r = -T^{rr}. The tree writes the surface term as 4 pi R^3 <T^r_r>(R) (tolman.py:135) in its mostly-plus convention, where T^r_r = T^{rr} = p_r. The upper-index spatial block is the pressure tensor in both conventions: Wang Sect. 4 gives T^{ii} = 0.5 eps0 E^2 = W_em for electrostatics, i.e. traceless with T^{ij} = -(Maxwell stress). So the tree's reading is correct in its convention (C8), and a reader moving between the two sources has to flip the sign of the mixed component.

LABEL DISCREPANCY -- tolman.py:128-130 calls eq. (20) 'von Laue's theorem ... in its finite-volume form'. In Wang, 'von Laue's theorem' is the four-vector criterion, eqs. (1)-(3) (Sect. 2), and eq. (20) is a Sect. 6 lemma relating divergence to that criterion. The content the tree takes, that the volume integral of the stress is a surface term, is what eq. (20) says. Giulini 1808.09320 eqs. (18)-(19) and Pinto & Avelino 2502.10427 eq. (24) present the same identity as the step that yields the von Laue condition, so the loose label has precedent. Recorded, not a content error.

INTERNAL STATUS DISCREPANCY -- tolman.py:145-146 says the equation was 're-read at source by this repair pass (Wang, Can. J. Phys. 93, 1470 (2015), eq. (20))', but the prior-art ledger row tolman.py:2522-2523 gives only 'read at source by the prior-art pass'. The two status sentences in the same file disagree about how many at-source reads there were. This audit READ eq. (20) at source a further time and confirms the orientation the repair pass restored: the surface integral is on the LEFT.

CITATION CHECK, CONFIRMED -- tolman.py:150-157 records that Wang's ref. [1] prints 'Ann. Phys. 35, 524 (1911)' against the tree's 'Ann. Phys. 340(8), 524 (1911)'. READ: Wang ref. [1] is 'M. von Laue. Ann. Phys. 35, 524 (1911).' Giulini 1808.09320 ref. [17] prints 'Annalen der Physik, 340(8):524-542, 1911'. Both numberings are attested at source, and the tree's decision to give both stands.

data_at_publication.quantity: none. Eq. (20) is a Gauss-divergence identity plus the product rule, with no numerical input; the trace step and the plate numbers (W5: p_t=-5, p_z=+1) are the tree's own exact fixtures, not measured data
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: no. There is no datum for the conclusion to move with.

rederivation.outcome: 16/16 exact checks pass (exit 0). C1: the GENERAL eq. (20), divergence term kept, holds with residual 0 on a ball for all 12 (i,mu) pairs of a generic non-symmetric, non-divergence-free polynomial tensor. C2: the same on the cube [-1,1]^3, so (20) does not need a ball. C1b (vacuity guard): the tree's short form FAILS without divergence-free, with residual int (d_l Omega^{l mu}) X^i = 28 pi R^5/15. C3: a NON-constant, NON-spherical, divergence-free symmetric stress built from a Maxwell stress function (phi = x^3 y + 2y^2 z^2 - x z^3 + x^2 y z + 3z^4) satisfies the short form for all 9 (i,j), and traced it gives 4 pi R^3 <T^r_r>(R) = int_V Theta^{ii} = 352 pi R^5/15. Its single-direction read (T_zz at the pole = 4R^2) differs from the angular average (88R^2/15). This extends, at the level of the flat identity only, the witness family the tree records as a gap at tolman.py:576-578; it says nothing about the tree's realisability layer. C4: <T^r_r> = (2p_t+p_z)/3 (tolman F3); W5 gives <T^r_r> = -3, e = -9, m = eV = 4 pi R^3 <T^r_r> < 0 with p_z = +1 > 0 (tolman F6); the raw-cell misread factor is exactly 9 (tolman.py:555-557). C5: Coulomb stress satisfies the identity exactly on a shell (both sides q^2(R-a)/(8 pi R a)), but on the ball LHS = -q^2/(8 pi R) and RHS = +infinity, so regularity is load-bearing. C6: for a conserved but time-dependent tensor the short form fails by exactly int(-d_t Theta^{00}) X^i (8 pi R^5 cos(omega t)/15 for the fixture), so time-independence is load-bearing. C7: for a non-symmetric tensor, left-divergence-free does not give the second-index (eq. 21) short form. C8: T^1_1 = -T^{11} in Wang's diag(-1,-1,-1,+1) and +T^{11} in mostly-plus. Two first-draft fixture errors in the script (a parity-vanishing C6 field and a C7 tensor that was not left-divergence-free), plus a Piecewise from a real omega, were found by the script failing. The fixtures were replaced and the replacements are commented in place. None of these concerned the source.

later_literature.ref: D. Giulini, 'Laue's Theorem Revisited: Energy-Momentum Tensors, Symmetries, and the Habitat of Globally Conserved Quantities', arXiv:1808.09320 (2018), Sect. 1.5 eqs. (18)-(20), Theorem 1
later_literature.what: Gives the same identity independently: d_n(T^{mu n} phi) = (d_n T^{mu n}) phi + T^{mu n} d_n phi with phi smooth, and then, 'if we assume energy-momentum conservation (3) and stationarity (14)', Gauss's theorem gives int_Sigma T^{mu n} d_n phi = int_{dSigma} T^{mu n} phi nu_n do. With phi = x^m this is the tree's short form of Wang (20). Two refinements. (i) Stationarity dT/dx^0 = 0 is enough; Laue's T^{0m} = 0 is not needed for this step, which matches the tree's hypotheses. (ii) The boundary term vanishes only if T vanishes on dSigma or falls off faster than 1/r^3. That is the flat parent of the tree's finite-radius use, where the boundary term is kept and IS the quantity read.

later_literature.ref: D. Giulini, arXiv:1808.09320, footnote 5 (p. 13) on Wang [28] = Can. J. Phys. 93, 1470 (2015)
later_literature.what: Giulini writes that Wang's derivation 'is itself logically incomplete': the third line of Wang's eq. (6) moves the integration domain from the hyperplane t' = const to t = const, which 'does not follow from the initial hypothesis of t-independence, unless some form of local energy-momentum conservation is imposed in addition'. This contests Wang's Sect. 2 proof of the necessary-and-sufficient von Laue theorem, and by extension his Sect. 4-5 verdicts that the Landau-Lifshitz and Weinberg versions are 'flawed'. Giulini Sect. 1.6 explains the Coulomb and container examples instead as violating Laue 'completeness' (conservation fails at the charges, or the boundary term is nonzero). It does NOT touch eq. (20), a Gauss-law identity that the tree alone uses. It is a caution for the tree: Wang's other claims should not be imported on his authority.

later_literature.ref: S. R. Pinto & P. P. Avelino, 'Deviations from the von Laue condition: Implications for the on-shell Lagrangian of particles and fluids', arXiv:2502.10427v2 (2025), Sect. III eqs. (22)-(27), Sect. VI eqs. (39)-(43)
later_literature.what:
Eq. (24) restates the identity, int_Sigma T^{mu j} delta^i_j d^3x = int_{dSigma} T^{mu j} x^i n_j dS, 'for a time-independent energy-momentum tensor' with d_j T^{mu j} = 0 (signature -,+,+,+, the same convention as the tree). Sect. VI then bounds the finite-radius residual under the dominant energy condition: |

_r/_r| <= m_out(r)/(m - m_out(r)) (eq. 42). This is a finite-volume companion to the tree's use and needs DEC, which the tree does not assume, so it does not transfer to the tree's DEC-violating sources.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: it has no purchase here, and the evidence runs against it. Eq. (20) is a mathematical identity: the product rule plus the three-dimensional divergence theorem, applied to a time-independent tensor. It takes no measured input, so there is no datum Wang (2012 arXiv / 2015 CJP) could have lacked. Evidence either way: (a) it is re-derived exactly here on a ball and on a cube, for a generic non-symmetric non-divergence-free tensor and for a non-constant non-spherical divergence-free one (16/16 checks); (b) it is restated independently by Giulini (2018, eqs. 18-19) and Pinto & Avelino (2025, eq. 24). What later work does add is SCOPE, not data. Giulini makes the boundary/fall-off conditions and the stationarity-versus-staticity distinction explicit, and he contests Wang's separate Sect. 2 necessity proof (footnote 5). The tree does not use that proof, and nothing in it bears on eq. (20). The limits that matter to the tree are hypotheses, not data: regularity throughout V (C5), time-independence (C6), symmetry or index order (C7) and sign convention (C8). Each is now a NAMED hypothesis with a computed failure case.
grade_evidence: The statement the tree uses (tolman.py:131-138), 'for a divergence-free time-independent tensor, oint_S dS_l(Theta^{l mu} X^i) = int_V Theta^{i mu} d^3x', traced on a sphere to give 4 pi R^3 <T^r_r>(R) = int_V Theta^{ii}, is the divergence-free specialization of the published eq. (20). Wang makes the same specialization himself in Sect. 6. It is READ at source (arXiv:1206.5618v12 = CJP 93, 1470), with the surface integral on the LEFT, as the tree's repair note says. It is machine-checked exactly: rederive/1206.5618.py, 16/16 pass, including the vacuity guard showing the divergence-free hypothesis is load-bearing. It has no data input. The tree's downstream fixtures that rest on it (F3's (2p_t+p_z)/3, W5's -3/-9, the factor 9) recompute exactly. Recorded without changing the grade: (1) tolman.py:566-567 over-states what (20) needs ('the REGION to be a ball'; the source allows any, even multiply connected, V). That is a discrepancy in the conservative direction and does not narrow any conclusion. (2) tolman.py:567 'THE SOURCE MAY BE ANYTHING' leaves regularity throughout V implicit in 'divergence-free' instead of naming it. The tree names it at tolman.py:1198 and 547-549 (regular_centre, ball_excludes_walls, Coulomb refusal), but as a centre condition, which is narrower than the throughout-V condition a non-spherical source needs. No site in the tree applies the identity to a source that violates it; its non-spherical witnesses are constant-stress. (3) The 'von Laue's theorem' label and the tolman.py:145-146 vs 2522-2523 status wording are discrepancies, not errors. (4) Wang's OTHER claims (the necessity proof, and 'Landau-Lifshitz/Weinberg flawed') are contested by Giulini 2018 fn. 5. The tree does not rest on them and must not start to. The grade is STANDS rather than NARROWED because the class the tree actually uses (balls; symmetric, time-independent, regular, conserved sources) lies inside the source's class. If the canonical entry's 'source of any shape' were read as licensing singular or walled sources, drift (2) would become a NARROWED; as the tree applies it, it does not.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if any tolman.py site, or a peer that imports SOURCE_SPHERICITY_IS_LOAD_BEARING=False, applies the Laue route to a source with an interior (including off-centre) singularity, a non-integrable stress, or a wall carrying surface force inside the ball. C5 computes that the identity fails there, and 'regular_centre' as defined does not exclude an off-centre singularity. The same holds for a time-dependent source (C6) or a non-symmetric tensor contracted on its second index (C7). DISCREPANCY-only changes would follow from finding that the arXiv version the prior-art pass read numbers the identity differently from v12/CJP (not checkable here: alphaXiv serves v12 only), or from a glyph-level read of eq. (20) that contradicts the operator recovery, which C1/C2 make very unlikely because any other operator choice fails the product rule. WRONG would need a counterexample to the divergence theorem under its hypotheses, which is not expected.
